bug_semantics: rConfig deliberately disabled self-registration with Auth::routes(['register' => false]), but a later bare Auth::routes() registered Laravel's default POST /register route again. An unauthenticated request could therefore reach RegisterController, whose create() inserted name, email, and password without a role; the users.role database default was Admin. The framework registration trait then authenticated the newly created full-Administrator account, exposing device credentials, users, and API-token functionality without invitation, approval, or email verification.
flaw_origin: Commit 5ae01b3781de867baad1a8aa8aebfc3448812f68 is the smallest true BIC: during the multiple-SSO-provider feature it directly added the second bare Auth::routes(); below the already restrictive call in routes/web.php. Its sole parent 6202a5d9e061fce98de25ec8b62a4973c0dffd35 has the restrictive call, RegisterController, and the pre-existing Admin role default, but no second bare call, so registration is not exposed there. This is a one-parent source-writing commit, not a move, revert, release commit, or merge; no separately represented squash members are needed or available for decomposition.
ai_marker: Absent on BIC 5ae01b3781de867baad1a8aa8aebfc3448812f68. `git cat-file commit 5ae01b3781de867baad1a8aa8aebfc3448812f68` shows author and committer danielrConfig <daniel@rconfig.com>, one parent, the SSO feature message, and no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI trailer, or bot identity. The Claude Co-Authored-By trailer is only on the later fix and is excluded by the BIC-only rule.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/rconfig/rconfig/security/advisories/GHSA-w3hx-9cxg-5ccr describes the duplicate-route/Admin-default chain, affected >=8.0.0,<8.2.10, and patched 8.2.10. In the validated clone, `git log -L '/Auth::routes();/,+1':routes/web.php 5ae01b3781de867baad1a8aa8aebfc3448812f68` attributes the exact added line to 5ae01b3781de867baad1a8aa8aebfc3448812f68; `git log -S'Auth::routes();' -- routes/web.php` independently shows its addition and d3fe04fc9d2e1f892b9e21f037e4104badd565e3 removal. `git grep -n -F 'Auth::routes();' 6202a5d9e061fce98de25ec8b62a4973c0dffd35 -- routes/web.php` returns no match, while the same command at 5ae01b3781de867baad1a8aa8aebfc3448812f68 returns routes/web.php:19; both revisions retain Auth::routes(['register' => false]) at line 8. `git show 6202a5d9e061fce98de25ec8b62a4973c0dffd35:app/Http/Controllers/Auth/RegisterController.php` shows create() omitting role, and `git log -S"default('Admin')" -- database` traces the fail-open default to the repository root snapshot. `git show d3fe04fc9d2e1f892b9e21f037e4104badd565e3 -- routes/web.php composer.json config/app.php database/migrations/2026_08_01_070306_update_users_role_default_to_user.php` shows the direct fix removing the bare call, changing the default to User, and bumping 8.2.9 to 8.2.10. The annotated core-8.2.10 tag peels to merge da649a1c22c2bc75adeda9e62daef24e3cd84903, whose second parent is d3fe04fc9d2e1f892b9e21f037e4104badd565e3. `git grep` finds the bare call in core-8.0.0 and core-8.2.9 but not core-8.2.10. Thus repository history and the repository advisory establish >=8.0.0,<8.2.10 despite the later global alias summary's broader 'before 8.2.13' wording.
reasoning: The pre-existing Admin column default was dangerous but not remotely reachable through self-registration once dc7d6285854a36acef7757e6131e383404680bd3 disabled registration. The smallest causal change that opened the unauthenticated attack path is therefore the second bare Auth::routes() line in 5ae01b3781de867baad1a8aa8aebfc3448812f68, not the root import, the disable-registration commit, a later refactor, the release merge, or the defense-in-depth default change. The immediate parent directly lacks that line. The direct source fix is d3fe04fc9d2e1f892b9e21f037e4104badd565e3 and first ships in core-8.2.10. Because the BIC commit object has no qualifying AI attribution and a human author/committer, the closed verdict is NOT_AI; AI attribution on the fix cannot change that result.
